summary: Albert Grünwedel worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Munich (1876–1883) and had a career at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin from 1881, serving as Director (1904–1921).

Albert Hoefer worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Greifswald, Göttingen, and the Humboldt University of Berlin (doctorate 1832–1837; habilitation ~1839–1840). He spent his academic career at the University of Greifswald, serving as professor from around 1840 to 1883.
Albert Hofmann studied at the University of Zurich from around 1925 to 1929. He was employed at Novartis from approximately 1929 to 1971.

Albert Lutz is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied under Eberhard Fischer and Helmut Brinker at the University of Zurich (~1974–1983). He worked at Museum Rietberg as curator for Chinese art (1982) and director (1998–2019).

Albert Schweitzer worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Strasbourg (~1893–1900) under Wilhelm Deecke, as well as at Tübingen and Prague. He held an academic post at the University of Strasbourg from approximately 1902 to 1913.

Albert Sechehaye was a linguist who studied at the University of Geneva (~1888–1893) under Ferdinand de Saussure. He subsequently held a post at the University of Geneva from approximately 1903 to 1946.

Albert Thumb was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He completed his habilitation at the University of Freiburg (~1888–1891) and held posts at Freiburg (1891, 1895), the University of Marburg (~1901–1909), and the University of Strasbourg (1909).

Albert Welter works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at McMaster University (~1980–1986) under Koichi Shinohara. He held posts at the University of Winnipeg (~1995–2014) and the University of Arizona (from 2013).
Alberto Todeschini works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held a guest post at Kyoto University and is attested at the Italian School of East Asian Studies in 2010.

Albion Moonlight Butters works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Columbia University, where he earned a PhD by 2006 under the supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman.

Albrecht Hanisch works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Marburg by 2000 under Michael Hahn, later serving as Acting Director of the Nepal Research Centre and Local Representative for the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.

Albrecht Weber was an Indologist who studied at Breslau, Bonn, and Humboldt University of Berlin (1842–1845). He served as a Privatdozent and adjunct professor of ancient Indian language and literature at Humboldt University of Berlin across 1848 to 1901.

Albrecht Wezler was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Dr. phil. at Tübingen (~1960–1965) under Paul Thieme and served as Director at the University of Hamburg (1973–2003) and Director of the Nepal Research Centre (1982–2004).

Aleix Ruiz-Falqués works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at Cambridge by 2016 under Eivind Kahrs and has held posts at Shan State Buddhist University, Singapore University of Technology and Design, and the Pali Text Society.

Aleksander Brückner was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Lviv, Vienna, and Frederick William University Berlin under August Leskien, subsequently holding academic posts at the University of Lviv (~1878–1881) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1881–1924).
Alessandro Giudice is an Indologist with posts attested in 2026 at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities as a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter and at the University of Munich as Dr.

Alessandro Graheli is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He has held positions at the University of Vienna and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2022), and at the University of Toronto (attested 2026).
Alex McKay is a historian, archaeologist, and Tibetologist. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London by 1995 and held a research fellowship at University College London.

Alex Watson works in Indology and philosophy, having studied at Oxford and SOAS, supervised by Alexis Sanderson and Harunaga Isaacson. His posts include Wolfson College, Oxford, Preceptor in Sanskrit at Harvard, and Professor of Indian Philosophy at Ashoka University.

Alex Wayman was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at UC Berkeley (~1950–1959) under Ferdinand Lessing. He taught at UC Berkeley, Wisconsin-Madison (~1961–1967), and Columbia University (1967–1991).
